parse.desc: parse_int_header then mystrtou32_modulo; base 16 after &h or 0x, else base 10; value reduced modulo 2**32; 0 when no digit is read
GetInt: optional &h or 0x selects %x, else %d; swscanf into int; throws on no match

post.desc: stored value is the visible value
percent value, divided by 100 at or before use
1 becomes 0 and 3 becomes 1; every other value becomes 0

stylefield.name: name
stylefield.note: Both renderers strip leading '*' characters. The stored name is not equivalent. libass keeps the bytes and replaces only an empty name with "Default" (ass.c:744-747). xy replaces an empty name with "Default" and maps the name "default" to "Default" without regard to case (STS.cpp:2263,1479). VSFilterMod also replaces an empty name through AddStyle. Name resolution therefore differs for mixed-case and empty names. The matrix records the conversion; it does not resolve the lookup.

stylefield.name: fontname
stylefield.note: Every renderer keeps the name text. VSFilterMod passes the name through WToT (STS.cpp:1862, TextFile.cpp:567-573). The pinned VSFilterMod project sets CharacterSet Unicode (subtitles.vcxproj:35), so WToT is the identity for that build and no character changes. A narrow-character build would truncate each wide character. The build scope is unknown by default.

stylefield.name: primarycolour
stylefield.note: assx checks only that the value is a valid hexadecimal RGB colour. It does not check cross-renderer equivalence of the stored form. libass byte-swaps at parse (parse_color_header, ass.c:338-342) and reads channels with the _r/_g/_b/_a macros (ass_parse.h:26-29). xy stores the integer as a COLORREF and reverses red and blue at use (RTS.cpp:59-62,1278-1328). The byte order was not followed to the drawn pixel, and that check is out of scope by decision.

stylefield.name: secondarycolour
stylefield.note: Same valid-value rule as primarycolour. Byte-order equivalence is out of scope.

stylefield.name: outlinecolour
stylefield.note: libass reads the SSA TertiaryColour name here (ass.c:694). In SSA, libass then overwrites OutlineColour from BackColour (ass.c:696-697). The v4+ path does not. Byte-order equivalence is out of scope.

stylefield.name: backcolour
stylefield.note: Same valid-value rule as primarycolour. Byte-order equivalence is out of scope.

stylefield.name: bold
stylefield.note: Every renderer applies !! to the integer, so any nonzero value becomes 1. Garbage input differs: libass yields 0 (ass.c:299) while GetInt throws (STS.cpp:1249). ASS022 already reports the malformed case.

stylefield.name: italic
stylefield.note: Same boolean rule as bold.

stylefield.name: underline
stylefield.note: Same boolean rule as bold. xy and VSFilterMod read this field only for sver 5 and later.

stylefield.name: strikeout
stylefield.note: Same boolean rule as bold. xy and VSFilterMod read this field only for sver 5 and later.

stylefield.name: fontsize
stylefield.note: libass stores a double. xy and VSFilterMod store a 32-bit float. A value with more than seven significant digits can round differently. ASS012 reports that case. The conversion is value-dependent, so the comparison resolves per value.

stylefield.name: scalex
stylefield.note: libass divides by 100 at parse. xy and VSFilterMod store percent and divide by 100 at use (RTS.cpp:430-431,736). All three clamp negatives to 0. The ratio is equivalent for a value that survives the float32 step.

stylefield.name: scaley
stylefield.note: Same rule as scalex.

stylefield.name: spacing
stylefield.note: Ignored by decision. assx does not check this field. The negative clamp is build-conditional in VSFilterMod. The clamp sits inside #ifndef _VSMOD (patch f002, STS.cpp:1899-1901), so a _VSMOD build keeps a negative spacing. A mod-build-version question cannot be resolved from the pinned source alone, so this field stays unmodeled for VSFilterMod.

stylefield.name: angle
stylefield.note: Same double versus float32 question as fontsize. No clamp in either renderer.

stylefield.name: outline
stylefield.note: All three clamp negatives to 0. Same float32 precision question as fontsize.

stylefield.name: shadow
stylefield.note: All three clamp negatives to 0. Same float32 precision question as fontsize.

stylefield.name: borderstyle
stylefield.note: Deferred by decision. assx does not check this field yet. libass keeps the raw integer and tests 3 for an opaque box and 4 for a background box (ass_render.c:2467,3009). xy and VSFilterMod map 1 to 0 and 3 to 1, and map every other value to 0. Values 1 and 3 agree. Value 4 selects a background box in libass and a plain outline in xy. Value 2 selects an outline in both. The conversion is value-dependent. Any future check must decide the accepted set from this note; the conversion is not equivalence-proven.

stylefield.name: alignment
stylefield.note: assx checks only that the value is in 1 to 9. It does not check cross-renderer equivalence. libass maps the value to HALIGN|VALIGN with numpad2align at parse (ass.c:712). xy and VSFilterMod keep the raw integer and derive the position at use from val%3 and val<=3 or val<=6 (RTS.cpp:3264-3268). The two derivations were shown to agree for values 1 to 9 only. Values 0, values above 9 and negative values are not accepted by this check and were not investigated.

stylefield.name: marginl
stylefield.note: Both renderers store one integer with no post-processing. libass reduces modulo 2**32 (ass.c:292-321). GetInt uses swscanf, whose overflow behavior is undefined. A value inside the int32 range is equivalent.

stylefield.name: marginr
stylefield.note: Same integer rule as marginl.

stylefield.name: marginv
stylefield.note: Same integer rule as marginl.

stylefield.name: encoding
stylefield.note: Same integer rule as marginl. libass stores it in Encoding (ass_render.c:1110).

stylefield.name: tertiarycolour
stylefield.note: SSA only. libass reads the name as OutlineColour, then overwrites OutlineColour from BackColour (ass.c:694-697). xy and VSFilterMod copy BackColour into colours[2] (STS.cpp:1532,1885). The two paths reach the same slot by different routes. The byte-order question from primarycolour also applies.

stylefield.name: alphalevel
stylefield.note: SSA only. libass applies the alpha to the three front colours and forces the back alpha to 0x80 (ass.c:533-541,733-734). xy and VSFilterMod clamp the value to 0..0xff and set alpha[3] to 0x80 (STS.cpp:1533-1534, 1886-1891). Both clamp to one byte, so a value inside 0..255 is equivalent.

stylefield.name: justify
stylefield.note: Retained, not an issue. libass parses Justify (ass.c:615) but no pinned reader was found for the stored value. xy and VSFilterMod have no Justify field at all. The field stays unmodeled and assx reports nothing for it.
